paragraphs.sourceText: Contrary to popular belief, older people generally do not want to live with their children. Moreover, most adult children 26 every bit as much care and support to their aging parents as was the case in the “good old days”, and most older people do not feel 27 .
paragraphs.translationZh: 与普遍看法相反，老年人通常不愿意与孩子住在一起。此外，大多数成年子女对年迈的父母提供的照顾和支持与“过去的美好时光”一样多，大多数老年人并没有感到被遗弃的感觉。

paragraphs.sourceText: About 80% of people 65years and older have living children, and about 90% of them have 28 contact with their children. About 75% of elderly parents who don’t go to nursing homes live within 30 minutes of at least one of their children.
paragraphs.translationZh: 65岁及以上的人中约有80%有活着的孩子，其中约90%的人与孩子有频繁接触。大约 75% 不去疗养院的老年父母与至少一名孩子的居住时间不超过 30 分钟。

paragraphs.sourceText: However, 29 having contact with children does not guarantee happiness in old age. In fact, some research has found that people who are most involved with their families have the lowest spirits. This research may be 30 , however, as ill health often makes older people more 31 and thereby increases contact with family members. So it is more likely that poor health, not just family involvement, 32 spirits.
paragraphs.translationZh: 然而，仅仅与孩子接触并不能保证晚年的幸福。事实上，一些研究发现，与家庭关系最密切的人情绪最低落。然而，这项研究可能存在偏见，因为健康状况不佳往往会使老年人更加依赖他人，从而增加与家人的接触。因此，更可能的是，健康状况不佳，而不仅仅是家庭的参与，抑制了人们的精神。

paragraphs.sourceText: Increasingly, researchers have begun to look at the quality of relationships, rather than at the frequency of contact, between the elderly and their children. If parents and children share interests and values and agree on childrearing practices and religious 33 , they are likely to enjoy each other’s company. Disagreements on such matters can 34 cause problems. If parents are agreed by their daughter’s divorce, dislike her new husband, and disapprove of how she is raising their grandchildren, 35 are that they are not going to enjoy her visits.
paragraphs.translationZh: 研究人员越来越多地开始关注老年人与其子女之间的关系质量，而不是接触频率。如果父母和孩子有共同的兴趣和价值观，并在养育子女的做法和宗教信仰上达成一致，他们很可能会享受彼此的陪伴。在这些问题上的分歧可能会导致问题，这是可以理解的。如果父母同意女儿离婚，不喜欢她的新丈夫，不同意她抚养孙子的方式，那么他们很可能不会喜欢她的探访。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: Could Food Shortages Bring Down Civilization?
paragraphs.translationZh: 粮食短缺会导致文明崩溃吗？

paragraphs.sourceText: A) For many years I have studied global agricultural, population, environmental and economic trends and their interactions. The combined effects of those trends and the political tensions they generate point to the breakdown of governments and societies. Yet I, too, have resisted the idea that food shortages could bring down not only individual governments but also our global civilization.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 多年来，我研究了全球农业、人口、环境和经济趋势及其相互作用。这些趋势及其产生的政治紧张局势的综合影响导致政府和社会的崩溃。然而，我也反对这样的观点：粮食短缺不仅会导致个别政府垮台，还会导致我们的全球文明垮台。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) I can no longer ignore that risk. Our continuing failure to deal with the environmental declines that are undermining the world food economy forces me to conclude that such a collapse is possible.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 我不能再忽视这种风险。我们在应对破坏世界粮食经济的环境恶化方面持续失败，迫使我得出这样的结论：这种崩溃是可能的。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) As demand for food rises faster than supplies are growing, the resulting food-price inflation puts severe stress on the governments of many countries. Unable to buy grain or grow their own, hungry people take to the streets. Indeed, even before the steep climb in grain prices in 2008, the number of failing states was expanding. If the food situation continues to worsen, entire nations will break down at an ever increasing rate. In the 20th century the main threat to international security was superpower conflict; today it is failing states.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 由于食品需求的增长速度快于供应的增长速度，由此导致的食品价格上涨给许多国家的政府带来了巨大的压力。由于无法购买粮食或自己种植粮食，饥饿的人们走上街头。事实上，甚至在 2008 年粮食价格大幅上涨之前，失败国家的数量就在不断增加。如果粮食形势继续恶化，整个国家就会以越来越快的速度崩溃。 20世纪国际安全的主要威胁是超级大国冲突。今天，它是失败的国家。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) States fail when national governments can no longer provide personal security, food security and basic social services such as education and health care. When governments lose their control on power, law and order begin to disintegrate. After a point, countries can become so dangerous that food relief workers are no longer safe and their programs are halted. Failing states are of international concern because they are a source of terrorists, drugs, weapons and refugees(难民), threatening political stability everywhere.
paragraphs.translationZh: D）当国家政府无法再提供人身安全、粮食安全以及教育和医疗保健等基本社会服务时，国家就会失败。当政府失去对权力的控制时，法律和秩序就开始瓦解。过了某个时间点，国家就会变得非常危险，以至于粮食救援人员不再安全，他们的计划也会停止。失败的国家受到国际社会的关注，因为它们是恐怖分子、毒品、武器和难民的来源，威胁着各地的政治稳定。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) The surge in world grain prices in 2007 and 2008—and the threat they pose to food security——has a different, more troubling quality than the increases of the past. During the second half of the 20th century, grain prices rose dramatically several times. In 1972, for instance, the Soviets, recognizing their poor harvest early, quietly cornered the world wheat market. As a result, wheat prices elsewhere more than doubled, pulling rice and corn prices up with them. But this and other price shocks were event-driven——drought in the Soviet Union, crop-shrinking heat in the U.S. Corn Belt. And the rises were short-lived: prices typically returned to normal with the next harvest.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 2007 年和 2008 年世界粮食价格的飙升及其对粮食安全构成的威胁与过去的上涨相比，具有不同的、更令人不安的性质。 20世纪下半叶，粮食价格数次大幅上涨。例如，1972年，苏联人很早就意识到自己歉收，悄悄垄断了世界小麦市场。结果，其他地方的小麦价格上涨了一倍多，拉动大米和玉米价格随之上涨。但这次和其他价格冲击都是由事件驱动的——苏联的干旱、美国玉米种植带的农作物减产。而且这种上涨是短暂的：价格通常会在下一次收获时恢复正常。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) In contrast, the recent surge in world grain prices is trend-driven, making it unlikely to reverse without a reversal in the trends themselves. On the demand side, those trends include the ongoing addition of more than 70 million people a year, a growing number of people wanting to move up the food chain to consume highly grain-intensive meat products, and the massive diversion(转向) of U.S. grain to the production of bio-fuel.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 相比之下，近期世界粮食价格的飙升是趋势驱动的，如果趋势本身不逆转，价格就不太可能逆转。在需求方面，这些趋势包括每年持续增加超过 7000 万人，越来越多的人希望向食物链上游移动以消费谷物高度密集的肉类产品，以及美国谷物大规模转向生产生物燃料。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) As incomes rise among low-income consumers, the potential for further grain consumption is huge. But that potential pales beside the never-ending demand for crop-based fuels. A fourth of this year’s U.S. grain harvest will go to fuel cars.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 随着低收入消费者收入的增加，粮食进一步消费的潜力巨大。但与对农作物燃料永无休止的需求相比，这种潜力就显得黯然失色了。今年美国粮食收成的四分之一将用于燃料汽车。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) What about supply? The three environmental trends——the shortage of fresh water, the loss of topsoil and the rising temperatures——are making it increasingly hard to expand the world’s grain supply fast enough to keep up with demand. Of all those trends, however, the spread of water shortages poses the most immediate threat. The biggest challenge here is irrigation, which consumes 70% the world’s fresh water. Millions of irrigation wells in many countries are now pumping water out of underground sources faster than rainfall can refill them. The result is falling water tables( 地下水位) in countries with half the world’s people, including the three big grain producers——China, India and the U.S.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 供应情况如何？淡水短缺、表土流失和气温上升这三大环境趋势使得世界粮食供应越来越难以快速扩大以满足需求。然而，在所有这些趋势中，水资源短缺的蔓延构成了最直接的威胁。这里最大的挑战是灌溉，它消耗了世界 70% 的淡水。现在，许多国家数以百万计的灌溉井从地下水源中抽水的速度超过了降雨补充水的速度。其结果是占世界一半人口的国家地下水位下降，其中包括中国、印度和美国三大粮食生产国。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) As water tables have fallen and irrigation wells have gone dry, China’s wheat crop, the world’s largest, has declined by 8% since it peaked at 123 million tons in 1997. But water shortages are even more worrying in India. Millions of irrigation wells have significantly lowered water tables in almost every state.
paragraphs.translationZh: 一）由于地下水位下降和灌溉井干涸，中国作为世界第一大小麦产量，自1997年达到峰值1.23亿吨以来，已经减少了8%。但印度的缺水问题更令人担忧。几乎每个州数以百万计的灌溉井都显着降低了地下水位。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) As the world’s food security falls to pieces, individual countries acting in their own self-interest are actually worsening the troubles of many. The trend began in 2007, when leading wheat-exporting countries such as Russia and Argentina limited or banned their exports, in hopes of increasing local food supplies and thereby bringing down domestic food prices. Vietnam banned its exports for several months for the same reason. Such moves may eliminate the fears of those living in the exporting countries, but they are creating panic in importing countries that must rely on what is then left for export.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 随着世界粮食安全的崩溃，个别国家为了自身利益而采取的行动实际上加剧了许多国家的麻烦。这一趋势始于2007年，当时俄罗斯和阿根廷等主要小麦出口国限制或禁止出口，希望增加当地粮食供应，从而降低国内粮食价格。出于同样的原因，越南禁止其出口数月。这些举措可能会消除生活在出口国的人们的恐惧，但它们却在进口国中造成了恐慌，这些国家必须依赖剩下的出口产品。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) In response to those restrictions, grain-importing countries are trying to nail down long-term trade agreements that would lock up future grain supplies. Food-import anxiety is even leading to new efforts by food-importing countries to buy or lease farmland in other countries. In spite of such temporary measures, soaring food prices and spreading hunger in many other countries are beginning to break down the social order.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 为了应对这些限制，粮食进口国正在努力敲定长期贸易协定，以锁定未来的粮食供应。粮食进口焦虑甚至导致粮食进口国采取新的措施购买或租赁其他国家的农田。尽管采取了这些临时措施，但许多其他国家的粮食价格飙升和饥饿蔓延正开始破坏社会秩序。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) Since the current world food shortage is trend-driven, the environmental trends that cause it must be reversed. We must cut carbon emissions by 80% from their 2006 levels by 2020, stabilize the world’s population at eight billion by 2040, completely remove poverty, and restore forests and soils. There is nothing new about the four objectives. Indeed, we have made substantial progress in some parts of the world on at least one of these——the distribution of family-planning services and the associated shift to smaller families.
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 由于当前的世界粮食短缺是趋势驱动的，因此必须扭转造成这种短缺的环境趋势。我们必须到2020年将碳排放量比2006年减少80%，到2040年将世界人口稳定在80亿，彻底消除贫困，恢复森林和土壤。这四个目标并没有什么新意。事实上，我们在世界一些地区至少在其中一个方面取得了实质性进展——计划生育服务的分配以及相关的向小家庭的转变。

paragraphs.sourceText: M) For many in the development community, the four objectives were seen as positive, promoting development as long as they did not cost too much. Others saw them as politically correct and morally appropriate. Now a third and far more significant motivation presents itself: meeting these goals may be necessary to prevent the collapse of our civilization. Yet the cost we project for saving civilization would amount to less than $200 billion a year, 1/6 of current global military spending. In effect, our plan is the new security budget.
paragraphs.translationZh: M) 对于发展界的许多人来说，这四个目标被视为积极的，只要成本不高，就能促进发展。其他人则认为它们在政治上是正确的，在道德上是适当的。现在，第三个也是更重要的动机出现了：实现这些目标可能是防止我们文明崩溃的必要条件。然而，我们预计每年拯救文明的成本将不到 2000 亿美元，占当前全球军费开支的 1/6。实际上，我们的计划是新的安全预算。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36.The more recent steep climb in grain prices partly results from the fact that more and more people want to consume meat products.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36.最近谷物价格的急剧攀升部分是由于越来越多的人想要消费肉类产品。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. Social order is breaking down in many countries because of food shortages.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 由于粮食短缺，许多国家的社会秩序正在崩溃。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. Rather than superpower conflict, countries unable to cope with food shortages now constitute the main threat to world security.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 现在，世界安全的主要威胁不是超级大国冲突，而是无法应对粮食短缺的国家。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. Some parts of the world have seen successful implementation of family planning.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 世界一些地区成功实施了计划生育。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. The author has come to agree that food shortages could ultimately lead to the collapse of world civilization.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 作者逐渐同意，粮食短缺最终可能导致世界文明的崩溃。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. Increasing water shortages prove to be the biggest obstacle to boosting the world’s grain production.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 事实证明，日益严重的水资源短缺是提高世界粮食产量的最大障碍。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. The cost for saving our civilization would be considerably less than the world’s current military spending.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 拯救我们文明的成本将大大低于世界目前的军费开支。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. To lower domestic food prices, some countries limited or stopped their grain exports.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 为了降低国内粮食价格，一些国家限制或停止粮食出口。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. Environmental problems must be solved to ease the current global food shortage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 必须解决环境问题才能缓解当前的全球粮食短缺问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. A quarter of this year’s American grain harvest will be used to produce bio-fuel for cars.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 今年美国谷物收成的四分之一将用于生产汽车生物燃料。

For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Declining mental function is often seen as a problem of old age, but certain aspects of brain function actually begin their decline in young adulthood, a new study suggests.
paragraphs.translationZh: 一项新的研究表明，精神功能下降通常被视为老年问题，但大脑功能的某些方面实际上在成年早期就开始下降。

paragraphs.sourceText: The study, which followed more than 2,000 healthy adults between the ages of 18 and 60, found that certain mental functions—including measures of abstract reasoning, mental speed and puzzle-solving—started to dull as early as age 27.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这项研究对 2000 多名年龄在 18 岁到 60 岁之间的健康成年人进行了跟踪调查，结果发现，某些心理功能——包括抽象推理、思维速度和解谜能力——早在 27 岁时就开始变得迟钝。

paragraphs.sourceText: Dips in memory, meanwhile, generally became apparent around age 37.
paragraphs.translationZh: 与此同时，记忆力下降通常在 37 岁左右变得明显。

paragraphs.sourceText: On the other hand, indicators of a person’s accumulated knowledge—like performance on tests of vocabulary and general knowledge—kept improving with age, according to findings published in the journal Neurobiology of Aging.
paragraphs.translationZh: 另一方面，根据发表在《衰老神经生物学》杂志上的研究结果，一个人积累的知识的指标——比如词汇和常识测试的表现——随着年龄的增长而不断提高。

paragraphs.sourceText: The results do not mean that young adults need to start worrying about their memories. Most people’s minds function at a high level even in their later years, according to researcher Timothy Salthouse.
paragraphs.translationZh: 研究结果并不意味着年轻人需要开始担心他们的记忆力。研究人员蒂莫西·索尔豪斯表示，大多数人的思维即使在晚年也能保持较高水平。

paragraphs.sourceText: “These patterns suggest that some types of mental flexibility decrease relatively early in adulthood, but that the amount of knowledge one has, and the effectiveness of integrating it with one’s abilities, may increase throughout all of adulthood if there are no diseases,” Salthouse said in a news release.
paragraphs.translationZh: 索尔豪斯在一份新闻稿中说：“这些模式表明，某些类型的心理灵活性在成年早期相对下降，但如果没有疾病，一个人拥有的知识量以及将其与个人能力相结合的有效性可能会在整个成年期增加。”

paragraphs.sourceText: The study included healthy, educated adults who took standard tests of memory, reasoning and perception at the outset and at some point over the next seven years.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这项研究的对象是健康、受过教育的成年人，他们在研究开始时以及接下来七年的某个时候接受了标准的记忆、推理和感知测试。

paragraphs.sourceText: The tests are designed to detect subtle ( 细微的) changes in mental function, and involve solving puzzles, recalling words and details from stories, and identifying patterns in collections of letters and symbols.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这些测试旨在检测心理功能的微妙变化，包括解决谜题、回忆故事中的单词和细节，以及识别字母和符号集合中的模式。

paragraphs.sourceText: In general, Salthouse and his colleagues found, certain aspects of cognition (认知能力) generally started to decline in the late 20s to 30s.
paragraphs.translationZh: 索尔豪斯和他的同事发现，总的来说，认知能力的某些方面普遍在 20 多岁到 30 多岁之间开始下降。

paragraphs.sourceText: The findings shed light on normal age-related changes in mental function, which could aid in understanding the process of dementia (痴呆), according to the researchers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 研究人员表示，这些发现揭示了与年龄相关的正常心理功能变化，这可能有助于理解痴呆症的过程。

paragraphs.sourceText: “By following individuals over time,” Salthouse said, “we gain insight in cognition changes, and may possibly discover ways to slow the rate of decline.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 索尔豪斯说：“通过长期跟踪个人，我们可以深入了解认知变化，并可能找到减缓衰退速度的方法。”

paragraphs.sourceText: The researchers are currently analyzing the study participants’ health and lifestyle to see which factors might influence age-related cognitive changes.
paragraphs.translationZh: 研究人员目前正在分析研究参与者的健康和生活方式，看看哪些因素可能影响与年龄相关的认知变化。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: The most important thing in the news last week was the rising discussion in Nashville about the educational needs of children. The shorthand( 简写)educators use for this is “pre-K”—meaning instruction before kindergarten—and the big idea is to prepare 4-year-olds and even younger kids to be ready to succeed on their K-12 journey.
paragraphs.translationZh: 上周新闻中最重要的事情是纳什维尔关于儿童教育需求的讨论不断升温。教育工作者对此使用的简写是“pre-K”——意思是幼儿园之前的指导——其主要目的是让 4 岁甚至更小的孩子做好准备，在 K-12 旅程中取得成功。

paragraphs.sourceText: But it gets complicated. The concept has multiple forms, and scholars and policymakers argue about the shape, scope and cost of the ideal program.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但事情变得复杂了。这个概念有多种形式，学者和政策制定者对理想计划的形式、范围和成本争论不休。

paragraphs.sourceText: The federal Head Start program, launched 50 years ago, has served more than 30 million children. It was based on concepts developed at Vanderbilt University’s Peabody College by Susan Gray, the legendary pioneer in early childhood education research.
paragraphs.translationZh: 联邦启蒙计划于 50 年前启动，已为超过 3000 万儿童提供服务。它基于早期儿童教育研究的传奇先驱苏珊·格雷 (Susan Gray) 在范德比尔特大学皮博迪学院提出的概念。

paragraphs.sourceText: A new Peabody study of the Tennessee Voluntary Pre-K program reports that pre-K works, but the gains are not sustained through the third grade. It seems to me this highlights quality issues in elementary schools more than pre-K, and indicates longer-term success must connect pre-K with all the other issues related to educating a child.
paragraphs.translationZh: 皮博迪对田纳西州自愿学前班项目的一项新研究报告称，学前班确实有效，但效果并不能持续到三年级。在我看来，这比学前班更能凸显小学的质量问题，并表明长期成功必须将学前班与与教育儿童有关的所有其他问题联系起来。

paragraphs.sourceText: Pre-K is controversial. Some critics say it is a luxury and shouldn’t be free to families able to pay. Pre-K advocates insist it is proven and will succeed if integrated with the rest of the child’s schooling. I lean toward the latter view.
paragraphs.translationZh: 学前班是有争议的。一些批评者表示，这是一种奢侈品，不应该免费提供给有能力支付的家庭。学前班的倡导者坚称，它已被证明，如果与孩子的其他学校教育相结合，将会取得成功。我倾向于后一种观点。

paragraphs.sourceText: This is, in any case, the right conversation to be having now as Mayor Megan Barry takes office. She was the first candidate to speak out for strong pre-K programming. The important thing is for all of us to keep in mind the real goal and the longer, bigger picture.
paragraphs.translationZh: 无论如何，这是梅根·巴里市长上任后进行的正确对话。她是第一个公开支持强有力的学前教育项目的候选人。重要的是我们所有人都要牢记真正的目标和更长远、更大的愿景。

paragraphs.sourceText: The weight of the evidence is on the side of pre-K that early intervention (干预)works. What government has not yet found is the political will to put that understanding into full practice with a sequence of smart schooling that provides the early foundation.
paragraphs.translationZh: 有充分的证据表明早期干预是有效的。政府尚未找到将这种理解付诸实践的政治意愿，并通过一系列智能学校教育提供早期基础。

paragraphs.sourceText: For this purpose, our schools need both the talent and the organization to educate each child who arrives at the schoolhouse door. Some show up ready, but many do not at this critical time when young brains are developing rapidly.
paragraphs.translationZh: 为此，我们的学校需要人才和组织来教育每一个来到校舍门口的孩子。有些人已经做好了准备，但许多人在年轻大脑快速发育的关键时刻还没有做好准备。
